correctness.rationale: Every coset element aγ squares to the distinguished involution y, so all m outside elements have order 4 and pair into exactly m/2 cyclic subgroups. Each such C4 is maximal cyclic and covers only <y>, giving the exact edge formula ε(G)=ε(A)+m/2. The published nilpotent theorem gives ε(A)≥ε(C_m), with equality only for cyclic A. Writing m=2^a s and using the published coprime cyclic-edge product formula reduces the remaining difference to 2^(a-1)s-[τ(s)+ε(C_s)]. The prime-power and coprime-product argument proves τ(s)+ε(C_s)≤s, with the exact equality behavior needed to obtain m=2 or 6.

value.rationale: The result verifies a named edge-minimality conjecture on a natural infinite family of even-order groups that is generally nonnilpotent and therefore lies outside the conjecture source's theorem. It extends the known ordinary-dicyclic edge formula from cyclic kernels to arbitrary finite abelian kernels and gives a complete equality classification. The decomposition is structural and reusable, not a finite census or parameter substitution.
